goal: Connect the reusable Agent-assisted CGKN workflow directly to Codex as a globally discoverable personal skill and verify it in an isolated project.
acceptance_criteria: A validated use-cgkn skill is retained in the CGKN repository and discoverable from the user's global Codex skill location.
Explicit $use-cgkn invocation and implicit CGKN-specific routing are documented in UI metadata and tested in an isolated project.
Provider generation remains an explicitly requested follow-on through scripts/run_local_pipeline.py and real tests remain required before success is reported.
The skill does not launch nested codex exec, persist credentials, author a sealed Provider candidate, or add a generation or delivery path.
The skill initializes and prepares a target project through cgkn-agent, lets the active Codex task author only a bounded advisory draft, and seals it with the deterministic supervisor.

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

quality_metrics.measure: bounded Codex escalation usefulness and authority isolation
quality_metrics.target: a librarian-curated request and Codex response stay within configured budgets, preserve request identity, produce actionable guidance, and cannot assert formal evidence or delivery authority
quality_metrics.method: schema validation, deterministic contract tests, support-pipeline prompt tests, and an offline failed-generation replay

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

interface_expectations: The personal Codex skill resolves to the reviewed repository copy and is explicitly invocable as $use-cgkn.
The active Codex task consumes the bounded escalation and authors advisory draft support only; it never starts nested Codex or writes Provider candidate source.
Only the deterministic supervisor can seal the brief, and only scripts/run_local_pipeline.py may receive it for generation.
Provider credentials remain process-only, and network research is an explicit existing-route opt-in.

feedback: The global -cgkn skill, direct active-Codex request-to-brief flow, Provider dry-run handoff, and regressions pass; a newly started task may be required for UI re-enumeration and live generation still needs a process-only Provider credential.

worked: A user-level junction to one reviewed repository skill let Codex use the bounded supervisor directly without nested codex exec or duplicated skill content.
did_not_work: The already-running task's startup skill catalog cannot demonstrate post-start UI re-enumeration, and the WindowsApps codex executable remains inaccessible from PowerShell.
experiments: Start a fresh Codex task in an unrelated repository, invoke -cgkn explicitly, and run one credentialed Provider generation when a process-only key is available.
